Submission of a request

Requests may involve sensitive personal data, including health data.
All processing must comply with applicable national and EU legal and ethical requirements.

title: Terms and conditions
text:
Terms and conditions
These Terms and Conditions apply as stipulated in the Agreement on the Supervision and Management of the Flemish HBM Database and Biobank (Overeenkomst inzake toezicht en beheer van de Vlaamse HBM Data- en Biobank), hereafter “Agreement TZC”

The lead-investigator(s) will be responsible for obtaining approval from a formally constituted and recognized Ethics Committee before the release of any data or samples can be approved by the Supervisory Board (TZC).
It is implied that the data provided are as complete and correct as possible, that any deficiencies are communicated to the lead-investigator(s), and that reasonable queries about individual cases in the dataset are answered.
Once permission has been granted, a similar set of data shall not be made available to any other multicenter study with the same objectives (unless notified to the Lead Investigator).
Data/samples released are to be used for the stated research only and any significant deviation from the research protocol must be agreed by the TZC.
Any corrections to data should be reported immediately to the chair of the TZC at TZC@provincieantwerpen.be
It is the responsibility of the Lead Investigator(s) to apply for funds to carry out the proposed study.
All data/samples released from the Flemish HBM studies should be treated as strictly confidential and stored securely to protect against illegal usage and theft.
No-one must attempt to discover the identity of any person within the supplied data or attempt to make contact with them or their family. Any reports of the findings of the defined research project will make no reference to individuals or make any statements which would allow individuals to be identified.
Data/samples released from the Flemish HBM studies will not be divulged to a third party. Data/samples released from the Flemish HBM studies will be stored and used in such a way that no unauthorized one can have access to it. Access to those data will be restricted to named personnel only.
After the above registry inclusion criterion are met, the data can be used for analysis. The methodology must clearly describe how missing data are handled.
On completion of the analysis the Lead Investigator’s registry may archive the dataset (in particular if revisions have been made to the dataset released) for up to 5 years from the release date of the data.
Maximum two years after the project has ended, the data, including new variables and new data, will be returned to VITO as the administrator of the Flemish HBM studies. The data will be destroyed locally. A renewed application will be made to the TZC to keep data longer than two years.
The TZC can request a short (no more than 2 A4 pages) progress report once a year during the course of the study. Any change in contact address or personnel during the research should be notified to the TZC.
The TZC can withdraw approval for use of data if the stated terms and conditions are studies will be administered by the legal advisors to Provinciaal Instituut voor Hygiëne (PIH).
The Lead Investigator indicates in detail (Annex 3) which variables/samples are needed for the analysis. VITO will provide the minimum dataset that is needed for the requested analysis, and these data will be pseudonymised.
To maximise internal valorisation of data, an embargo of 3 years will be applied for not yet published data.
Analysis of biobank samples will only be possible in partnership with the research teams who collected the initial samples. The analysis performed on the requested samples shall be subjected to authorization by the TZC, to ensure the maximum benefit will come from the samples retrieved from the biobank. Also to meet the required communication agreements that were made with the participants. Leftovers of biobank samples will be returned to the Flemish HBM Biobank.
Unless otherwise agreed upon in writing, all intellectual property rights to the Flemish HBM Database and the data contained therein are reserved to the parties who generated the data, as stipulated in Article 4 of the Agreement TZC (link toevoegen?).
Costs for obtaining Flemish HBM data or samples. It may be necessary to make an administrative charge to cover the cost of collecting/keeping/accessing the data/samples from the Flemish HBM Database or Biobank. The costs will depend on the nature and numbers of the data or samples required.
The TZC is entitled to request the inclusion of 2 co-authors, in accordance with Article 6.7 and Article 8.3 of the Agreement TZC.
Reporting results from research based on data or samples obtained from the Flemish HBM studies. If data acquired from the Flemish HBM studies or results from sample analysis is to be reported in any form of publication or official document, the manuscripts (or at least title, abstract and author list) must be communicated to the TZC at the latest 30 calendar days prior to submission for dissemination.
The data providers should be acknowledged in publications and scientific reports (link naar teksten toevoegen)
Some data (e.g. ethnicity, health data) are sensitive according to GDPR rules. For this data, specific agreements on publication policy and terms for communication to the supervisory board can be agreed upon in advance.

title: Data and/or Sample access request
text:
Access to biobanked samples and/or individual-level data of the Flemish HBM studies is granted on request and subject to approval.



Sample and/or Data access requests can be submitted by stakeholders for research projects in the public interest, in line with the objectives of the Flemish HBM studies.







Submits a Sample and/or Data Access Request Form


Via Microsoft Forms.

To preprare for a form submission, you may consult the corresponding word version [here][to be established].

Provide the required annexes via e-mail as instructed in the form.

Selection of studies
Selection of variables
Selection of samples



The request is reviewed by the Flemish Supervisory Board
If approved, access is granted:

to the requested Flemish HBM biobanked samples
to the requested subset of Flemish HBM data (studies and variables),
only after signature of the applicable agreements

Data Controller Agreement[LINK to be included]
Material Transfer Agreement[LINK to be included]


Approved samples are made available via the Biobank manager
Approved data extracts are made available via the Flemish HBM Data Platform manager (contact)





Download the Annex – Studies file(s) here.
For each study you request: - set request_stud_1isYes = 1
✅ All studies marked with request_stud_1isYes = 1 are included in the request.



Download the Annex – Variables file(s) here
For each variable you request: - set request_var_1isYes = 1
✅ All variables marked with request_var_1isYes = 1 are included in the request.



Download the Annex – Samples file(s) here.
For each sample type you request:

set request_sample_1isYes = 1
fill out: request_sample_volume - indicate the requested minimal volume per sample
fill out: request_sample_n - indicate the number of requested samples
fill out: request_sample_remarks - when applicable, provide remarks

✅ All studies marked with request_sample_1isYes = 1 are included in the request.




For questions on access to data and/or samples from the Flemish HBM Studies, contact the Flemish HBM supervisory board: TZC@provincieantwerpen.be
For assistance in submitting a request to obtain access to samples and/or data, contact: flehs.datamanagement@vito.be

title: Overview
text:
This section describes how to provide data to the PEH Data Platform.
It focuses on:

required input structures
data validation: supported checks and inspections
known limitations




Providing data to the PEH Data Platform typically follows these steps:

The data provider signs the Protocol
A codebook is prepared together with the data platform manager
The data platform build the project configuration in the PEH Data Platform
The data provider receives a tailored data template to provide the data
The data provider requests a user account to the PEH Data Platform
The data provider runs services in the PEH Data Platform on the filled out data template:


data validation
data enrichment
summary statistics


The data provider inspects the outputs and upon approval, proceeds to data upload to the PEH Data Platform











Important



The PEH Data Platform is a supporting tool.
It does not: - guarantee regulatory or ethical compliance - detect conceptual errors in study design - replace formal data submission checks


Responsibility for data quality remains with the data provider.

title: Data requirements
text:
This page describes the data requirements for using the PEH Data Platform.
It explains:

which data structures are expected
the role of templates and codebooks

This information is essential for correct and consistent use of the platform.


The PEH Data Platform assumes that data providers:

work with predefined data templates (dowload link will follow)
follow agreed codebooks (click to download)
take responsibility for data correctness and completeness

The platform supports inspection and harmonisation through data validation services, but does not enforce or modify data.


Codebooks describe the meaning and coding of variables, including:

variable definitions
allowed values or value domains
units and categories where applicable

They form the reference against which input data are inspected during the data validation in the PEH Data Platform






Note



The PEH Data platform does not harmonise or recode values automatically.








A template defines:
Input data should:




Templates and codebooks are complementary:

Templates define structure
Codebooks define semantics

Correct use of the PEH Data Platform requires alignment with both.







Important



Use of the PEH Data Platform does not shift responsibility for data quality.
Data providers remain responsible for:

correctness of their data
alignment with project specifications
ethical and regulatory compliance

title: Overview
text:
This section describes how to get access to biobanked samples and/or data of the Flemish HBM studies.
It focuses on:

Submission of a Sample and/or Data request




Requests may involve sensitive personal data, including health data.
All processing must comply with applicable national and EU legal and ethical requirements.

title: Sample request
text:
Access to biobanked samples of the Flemish HBM studies is granted on request and subject to approval.



Sample requests can be submitted for research projects in the public interest, in line with the objectives of the Flemish HBM studies. Along with the samples, data of the Flemish HBM studies can be requested [LINK to be included].







The RDC submits a Data Access Request Form


Via Microsoft Forms.

To preprare for a form submission, you may consult the corresponding word version [here][to be established].

Provides the required annexes as instructed in the form.

Selection of studies
Selection of samples: When applicable:
Selection of variables:



The request is reviewed by the Flemish Supervisory Board
If approved, access is granted:

to the requested biobanked Flemish HBM samples
when applicable, to the requested Flemish HBM data (studies and variables),
only after signature of the applicable agreement(s)(/datausers/agreement.html)


To avoid requesting data and/or samples for research questions that have already been explored, it is advised to browse the Publications section in this user guide prior to submitting your request.





The Data Access Request Form collects the following information.



Main project name (acronym and full name)
Research project title
Date of submission





Scientific background
Objective and specific research questions





Study design
Target population
(e.g. age groups, sex, inclusion/exclusion criteria)





Requested datasets and studies
Requested variables


📌 Requested data must be specified using the official annex files generated via this application.





Statistical methods and analytical models
Sensitivity or pooled analyses (if applicable)
Requirements for data comparability





Explicit declaration that only data strictly necessary to answer the research questions are requested





Responsible person and institution
Contact details
Data analysts and (if applicable) external data processors
Planned study start and end dates
Publication intentions






To complete a Data Access Request, two annex files are required.
Both must be downloaded from this application.



Download the Annex – Studies file(s) from Studies.
For each study you request: - set request_stud_1isYes = 1
✅ All studies marked with request_stud_1isYes = 1 are included in the request.




Download the Annex – Variables file(s) from the Codebooks
For each variable you request: - set request_var_1isYes = 1
✅ All variables marked with request_var_1isYes = 1 are included in the request.
⚠️ Only annex files generated and completed via the Studies and Codebooks sections of this application are accepted.





For questions regarding data availability or the data access procedure, please contact:
PEHDataPlatform@vito.be
